Guidance & outlook: In terms of our quarterly results, we are happy to announce that our first quarter revenue from operations closed at INR1,054 crores, an year-over-year increase of over 24%, in line with what we were expecting.
So, the results are amazing as expected and everything is in line with what we were Physicswallah Limited August 14, 2026 expecting this year.
While we did around INR847 odd crores in topline in Q1 FY26, the overall number that was there for FY26 was essentially INR3,900 odd crores.
Growth & demand: Revenue from online grew 33% year -over-year and offline and other businesses grew at 16%.

We do believe while NEET UG calendar shifted by 5 to 7 weeks this year, our collections post the results announcement on July 16 have been encouraging and we've seen almost 50% growth as compared to last year.
The online, if you see, the growth of online is we can witness at 33%, whereas the offline growth if you see it's growing at 14% because a large part of our offline comes from NEET examination.
Margins & costs: Given this seasonality, our first quarter pre-Ind AS EBITDA closed at negative INR44 crores, equating to 4%, with an improvement of 624 basis points from Q1 of last year.
EBITDA was positive in Q1, closed at INR52 crores compared to negative INR21 crores last year same period.
Our employee cost without ESOP cost were lower by 2.6% as compared to last year.
Capex & expansion: Our approach to offline expansion will be opportunistic and limited to geographies that fit into our cohort economics.
Apart from this, we were investing in a category called NEET PG, which may become a big category.
So, that remains the same in terms of categorical expansion or in terms of geographical expansion.
Balance sheet & cash: All of this happened through all our leverage coming through our cost items.
Also, our current quarter ESOP cost remained flat in line with what we had expensed in the first quarter of last year and gave us a leverage of 117 basis points.
We continue to see leverage on our distribution and marketing expenses.
Risks & challenges: So the outcome has never been a challenge in our online categories.
So, offline is the competition for the top results, online we are already winning the result vertical.

Just calling out Kota center here because the Kota specifically city has decline in terms of student inflow, but remaining all the centers are now delivering 13% to 15% margin profile at this point of time.

guidance.t: In terms of our quarterly results, we are happy to announce that our first quarter revenue from operations closed at INR1,054 crores, an year-over-year increase of over 24%, in line with what we were expecting.

Guidance & outlook: Our full-year revenue from operations closed at INR3,900 crores, an year-over-year increase of over 35%, in line with our expectations.
Our online revenues now contribute 50.1% of our overall revenues as compared to 48.6% in FY25.
And as well as part of our expansion in South from FY25 to FY26, there also we have done almost 100% improvement in collection.
Growth & demand: So we grew 39% in online revenues, and blended we grew by 35%.
Last quarter we launched Ask AI, more than 3 million queries have been solved by Ask AI, one of the most loved features which we have launched for the students.

Also, as communicated earlier to stock exchanges, our annual flagship event Vishwas Diwas concluded with 36% year-over-year growth in collections from our online business, 21% growth in enrolments, and 12% growth in ARPU for collections that were done during the Vishwas Diwas.
Margins & costs: If we talk about EBITDA, against INR93 crores EBITDA last year, we did INR300 crores of EBITDA, that is 3x jump in the EBITDA.
Our employee cost excluding ESOP cost was lower by 1% as compared to last year.

As I've mentioned couple of times in the past also, our playbook is to build communities in every category we get into, and we believe we will continue to get significant leverage on these costs as we scale up, with ambition of at least reducing this cost by 20% over the next three years, largely due to the impact of scale and efficiencies of spends.
Capex & expansion: We will continue to have a very balanced expansion strategy going forward on our offline expansion, with focus on improving profitability across all our offline channels and business.

In terms of our acquisition that we announced last quarter, we are very happy how the Saarthi acquisition is panning out, and we are already working on multiple synergies in terms of tech build and distribution leverage.
And the second question is with respect to the announcement that you made of a INR120 crores investment in a NBFC, a wholly owned company.
Balance sheet & cash: Our strong results showcase our operating leverage, not only in terms of our cost structures but also in terms of the growth that we've seen across all our education categories.
Our overall leverage on direct costs gave us 2.4% year-over- year benefit as we scale up and improve our operating leverage across all our businesses.
In terms of our cash flow generated from our operations, this year we generated over INR800 crores of cash flow from operations.
Risks & challenges: And this despite you mentioning in the letter that 4Q is typically a soft quarter.

guidance.t: Our full-year revenue from operations closed at INR3,900 crores, an year-over-year increase of over 35%, in line with our expectations.
Some of the centers have higher profitability on upwards of 20% as well, but blended is 13% to 15% is at a steady state margin is what we are aiming for.

Guidance & outlook: Our marketing spends dropped by almost like INR20 crores in this quarter and we expect a significant synergies coming in from the Q4 of last year to Q4 of this year.
We are looking at 70 centers next year with an outlay of INR200 crores.
On a full year basis we are anticipating that we will significantly be lower than the 9.6% that we spent last year.
Growth & demand: Overall revenue growth remained robust in Q3 FY‘26 with total revenue from operations reaching to INR1,082 crores, a 34% revenue increase year-over-year.
Revenue was clocked at INR2,980 crores, a 31% year-over-year increase and surpassed the full year revenue of last year of INR2,886 crores.
In terms of our breakup of our online and offline segment, our online segment grew at, now contributes almost like 51% and grew at 38% year-over-year.
Margins & costs: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA of INR219 crores translating to 20.2% margin.

In terms of the overall cost initiatives, the direct cost gave us a leverage of almost like 2.8% year-over-year obviously due to all the cost reduction initiatives that we ran, especially around the consultants and the professional fees.

Utkarsh Classes had a great year in reimagining the entire state exams business, they reported 6% pre-Ind AS EBITDA against a negative for last year and we will see significant amount of cost leverage continue to come in that business.
Capex & expansion: Moving on to the performance of our acquisitions, we are extremely bullish about our Sarrthi partnership and acquisition that we did last quarter in UPSC practice.
When we bought the acquisition, I think they were INR90 crores in top line.

These three categories put together this year for the first nine months have contributed INR32 crores and we will continue to invest in these new categories to actually, to get them to the goodness that we've seen in our earlier categories.
Balance sheet & cash: We generated almost INR600 crores from cash flow from operations in the first nine months.

Our overall tech spends because of the scale that we have grown last year, we see almost like a percentage leverage on the tech spends in spite of our AI pod cost of the tech and product team going up by 40% from last year.
The point I was earlier making in terms of leverage, if our last year marketing spends were INR276 crores which was roughly 9.6% of the last year revenues.
Risks & challenges: This quarter Sarrthi reported revenues of INR22 crores and EBITDA of INR15 crores, this is what we consolidated in our books and we can now surely say that our overall UPSC practice is now the market leader in terms of the overall, all our competition as well.
Their basics are so weak that it is a bit difficult to get outcomes from them.
Here is my competition is a local non-tech led schools where the curriculum and the standard practices are not there.

guidance.t: And when you say that margins would be 18% to 44%.

Guidance & outlook: We saw an ~8% increase in our online ACPU and we feel that our academic cycle, depending on how the enrollments come in, we expect the full year number to be in the same region.
Next year, when we take admission in the second year of operations, when it becomes ~2000, the same center starts giving us 6% of the margin.
So, the FTP mix in overall faculty, earlier it used to be ~10%, next year we increased it to ~18%, now it is around 27%, so this will go to next year ~35%.
Growth & demand: And overall, company is looking quite strong in terms of enrollment growth, in terms of overall revenue growth, path to profitability.
Our adjusted EBIDTA grew ~38% to INR269 crores with margin expansion from 23% to 26%.
So in H1, if we compare the growth of H1 from last year to H1, then we have a 29% growth of H1 from last year to this year.
Margins & costs: And in quarter 3, upwards of 20% EBITDA, which we have done in quarter 2, a number of 15% EBITDA.

In terms of your question of margin profile of both the businesses, at a steady state, offline business tends towards ~13% EBITDA level and in online business, our early exam categories are giving ~45% EBITDA, IGAAP EBITDA.
So, to give you steady state margins of online business is somewhere between ~35% to ~45% EBITDA and steady state margins for our offline business is ~13% - ~15% EBITDA.
Capex & expansion: On the, let's say, expansion into other -- both actually South as well as other than JEE and NEET, do you think you are spreading -- as an outsider, I feel you are spreading yourself a bit too thin.

At the same time, any M&A, the company looks at it from the length that either they give us a geographical expansion, that if we are not present in any geographical or specific language, then we do M&A there or they give us a categorical expansion.
The second question is on your offline expansion, if you give some understanding.
Balance sheet & cash: You can say, over the period of time, marketing costs will get leverage.
Payroll costs as a percentage of revenue will get leverage as well as trajectory for enrollment growth will start to look strong.
And there is a lot of leverage left from operational efficiencies.
Risks & challenges: In the future, if you see the percentage of H1 from 2025 to 2026, what is the percentage of total enrollment coming from JEE and NEET exam categories, that is also on decline.
What we did offline in 3.5 years, our competition took 40 years to achieve.
Do you just follow the competition and possibly put up a center there or like, there is some different strategy when you identify the Physicswallah Limited December 09, 2025 location for a center.

guidance.t: But since the top line is ~25%, in your opinion, in your waist I would have thought that offline will grow a little more.
